programme.title: Load Balancing & Auto Scaling Follow Along
programme.topic: AWS Elastic Load Balancing and EC2 Auto Scaling
programme.outcome: Configure an internet-facing Application Load Balancer, target group, launch template, multi-AZ Auto Scaling group, target tracking dynamic scaling policy and health checks; verify load distribution and controlled scale-out; then safely delete only the resources created by the lab.
programme.statusNotice: Offline authoring manuscript only — not locally validated, imported, accepted, approved, published or fingerprinted.
examCoverage: ELB health integration with Auto Scaling
completionDefinition: A dedicated two-AZ VPC and public network are created from nothing.
Internet HTTP reaches only fa-lba-alb-sg; backend HTTP is allowed only from the ALB security group.
fa-lba-tg checks /health and receives targets through fa-lba-asg.
fa-lba-lt defines the repeatable Amazon Linux 2023 web-server configuration.
fa-lba-asg starts with minimum 2, desired 2 and maximum 4 across eu-west-2a and eu-west-2b.
The ASG uses ELB health checks, a 120-second grace period and 120-second default instance warmup.
fa-lba-request-scaling tracks ALB request count per target with target value 50.
Controlled HTTP traffic demonstrates a scaling activity without allowing capacity above 4.
All chargeable compute/load-balancing resources are removed before credentials or local files.

tasks.title: Verify the training account and AWS CLI
tasks.goal: Confirm the disposable training account, AWS CLI and eu-west-2 Region before creating resources.
tasks.whyItMatters: A known-good identity and Region prevent later ALB/ASG errors being confused with account or CLI problems.
tasks.examRelevance: SAA-C03 covers high-performing elastic compute and appropriate load-balancing/scaling strategies.

browserSteps.instruction: Sign in to the AWS training account.
Confirm that no fa-lba resource already exists for this lab.
Open Windows PowerShell.
Run aws --version.
Do not create or use root access keys.
Root is used only for Task 2 bootstrap and final IAM-user removal.

tasks.title: Create the temporary Load Balancing and Auto Scaling IAM user
tasks.goal: Create fa-lba-admin, one temporary access key and the complete lab policy, then sign out of root.
tasks.whyItMatters: The identity needs explicit permissions for the VPC, launch template, ALB, target group and Auto Scaling group without AdministratorAccess.
tasks.examRelevance: Secure identity boundaries remain part of sound AWS architecture.
warnings: Several create APIs need broad resource scope before generated IDs exist; the policy uses exact action lists rather than service-wide wildcards and all lab resources use fa-lba names.

browserSteps.instruction: Sign in as root only for this bootstrap task.
Open IAM > Users > Create user.
Set User name to fa-lba-admin and enable console access.
Create the user.
Open IAM > Policies > Create policy > JSON.
Replace the editor with the complete fa-lba-admin-policy JSON below.
Create the policy with the exact name fa-lba-admin-policy.
Open fa-lba-admin > Add permissions > Attach policies directly.
Select fa-lba-admin-policy and attach it.
Open Security credentials and create one access key for CLI use.
Copy the values only to a temporary secure location.
Sign out of root.
Sign in as fa-lba-admin for all routine browser work.

editableBlocks.title: user-data.sh
editableBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash set -euxo pipefail dnf install -y httpd TOKEN=$(curl -sS -X PUT -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600" http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token) INSTANCE_ID=$(curl -sS -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: ${TOKEN}" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id) AZ=$(curl -sS -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: ${TOKEN}" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/placement/availability-zone) cat > /var/www/html/index.html < fa-lba

Load Balancing & Auto Scaling Follow Along

Instance: ${INSTANCE_ID}

Availability Zone: ${AZ}

EOF echo "healthy" > /var/www/html/health systemctl enable httpd systemctl start httpd

editableBlocks.title: generate-load.ps1

expectedResults: No credential appears in either file.

verificationChecks.text: The CLI profile works in eu-west-2.

tasks.title: Create the VPC, two public subnets, internet gateway and route table
tasks.goal: Create fa-lba-vpc with public subnets in eu-west-2a and eu-west-2b and a public default route.
tasks.whyItMatters: The ALB and ASG span two Availability Zones, and the instances need outbound internet for Apache installation.
tasks.examRelevance: Multi-AZ horizontal compute and load balancing improve resilience and elasticity.
warnings: Public IPv4 addresses and later ALB/EC2 resources can incur charges.

browserSteps.instruction: Open the VPC console and select Europe (London) eu-west-2.
Create VPC fa-lba-vpc with IPv4 CIDR 10.60.0.0/16.
Enable DNS hostnames for fa-lba-vpc.
Create fa-lba-public-a in eu-west-2a with 10.60.1.0/24.
Create fa-lba-public-b in eu-west-2b with 10.60.2.0/24.
For each subnet enable auto-assign public IPv4.
Create internet gateway fa-lba-igw.
Attach fa-lba-igw to fa-lba-vpc.
Create route table fa-lba-public-rt in fa-lba-vpc.
Add route 0.0.0.0/0 to fa-lba-igw.
Associate fa-lba-public-a and fa-lba-public-b with fa-lba-public-rt.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create VPC
cliBlocks.content: $VPC_ID = aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.60.0.0/16 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=vpc,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-lba-vpc},{Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-lba}]" --query Vpc.VpcId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - enable DNS hostnames
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 modify-vpc-attribute --vpc-id $VPC_ID --enable-dns-hostnames "{\"Value\":true}" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create subnet A
cliBlocks.content: $SUBNET_A_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.60.1.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-lba-public-a},{Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-lba}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create subnet B
cliBlocks.content: $SUBNET_B_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.60.2.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-lba-public-b},{Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-lba}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - public IPv4 subnet A
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 modify-subnet-attribute --subnet-id $SUBNET_A_ID --map-public-ip-on-launch --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - public IPv4 subnet B
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 modify-subnet-attribute --subnet-id $SUBNET_B_ID --map-public-ip-on-launch --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create internet gateway
cliBlocks.content: $IGW_ID = aws ec2 create-internet-gateway --tag-specifications "ResourceType=internet-gateway,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-lba-igw},{Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-lba}]" --query InternetGateway.InternetGatewayId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - attach internet gateway
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 attach-internet-gateway --internet-gateway-id $IGW_ID --vpc-id $VPC_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create route table
cliBlocks.content: $RT_ID = aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id $VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-lba-public-rt},{Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-lba}]" --query RouteTable.RouteTableId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create default route
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id $RT_ID --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --gateway-id $IGW_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - associate subnet A
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id $RT_ID --subnet-id $SUBNET_A_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - associate subnet B
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 associate-route-table --route-table-id $RT_ID --subnet-id $SUBNET_B_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

expectedResults: The two /24 subnets are in different AZs.
The route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 to fa-lba-igw.

tasks.title: Create separate ALB and web security groups
tasks.goal: Allow public HTTP only to the ALB and backend HTTP only from the ALB security group.
tasks.whyItMatters: The instances should not accept direct application traffic from the internet.
tasks.examRelevance: The common security pattern is client -> ALB SG -> application SG.

browserSteps.instruction: Open EC2 > Security Groups.
Create fa-lba-alb-sg in fa-lba-vpc with inbound HTTP TCP 80 from 0.0.0.0/0.
Keep the default allow-all outbound rule.
Create fa-lba-web-sg in fa-lba-vpc.
Add inbound HTTP TCP 80 with Source set to fa-lba-alb-sg.
Do not add SSH.
Keep the default allow-all outbound rule.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - rebuild VPC ID
cliBlocks.content: $VPC_ID = aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-lba-vpc --query "Vpcs[0].VpcId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create ALB SG
cliBlocks.content: $ALB_SG_ID = aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-lba-alb-sg --description "HTTP to training ALB" --vpc-id $VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=security-group,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-lba-alb-sg},{Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-lba}]" --query GroupId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - allow HTTP to ALB
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id $ALB_SG_ID --protocol tcp --port 80 --cidr 0.0.0.0/0 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create web SG
cliBlocks.content: $WEB_SG_ID = aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-lba-web-sg --description "HTTP from ALB only" --vpc-id $VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=security-group,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-lba-web-sg},{Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-lba}]" --query GroupId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - allow ALB to web
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id $WEB_SG_ID --protocol tcp --port 80 --source-group $ALB_SG_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

expectedResults: fa-lba-web-sg allows HTTP only from fa-lba-alb-sg.

verificationChecks.text: The web SG source is the ALB SG ID.

tasks.title: Create the target group and /health health check
tasks.goal: Create fa-lba-tg for instance targets on HTTP:80 with health path /health.
tasks.whyItMatters: The target group controls both backend routing and target health evaluation.
tasks.examRelevance: ALB health checks are configured per target group and only healthy targets receive normal traffic.

browserSteps.instruction: Open EC2 > Target Groups > Create target group.
Target type: Instances.
Name: fa-lba-tg.
Protocol HTTP, port 80, IPv4.
VPC: fa-lba-vpc.
Health check protocol HTTP.
Health check path /health.
Healthy threshold 2, unhealthy threshold 2, timeout 5 seconds, interval 30 seconds, success codes 200.
Do not manually register a target.
Create the target group.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - rebuild VPC ID
cliBlocks.content: $VPC_ID = aws ec2 describe-vpcs --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-lba-vpc --query "Vpcs[0].VpcId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create target group
cliBlocks.content: $TG_ARN = aws elbv2 create-target-group --name fa-lba-tg --protocol HTTP --port 80 --target-type instance --vpc-id $VPC_ID --health-check-protocol HTTP --health-check-path /health --health-check-port traffic-port --health-check-interval-seconds 30 --health-check-timeout-seconds 5 --healthy-threshold-count 2 --unhealthy-threshold-count 2 --matcher HttpCode=200 --tags Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-lba --query "TargetGroups[0].TargetGroupArn" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - describe target group
cliBlocks.content: aws elbv2 describe-target-groups --target-group-arns $TG_ARN --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

tasks.title: Create the launch template
tasks.goal: Create fa-lba-lt with Amazon Linux 2023, t3.micro, IMDSv2, fa-lba-web-sg and the supplied user data.
tasks.whyItMatters: All Auto Scaling instances should launch from one repeatable configuration.
tasks.examRelevance: Launch templates are the reusable EC2 configuration used when Auto Scaling adds capacity.
warnings: EC2 instances and public IPv4 addresses can incur charges.

browserSteps.instruction: Open EC2 > Launch Templates > Create launch template.
Name: fa-lba-lt.
Version description: fa-lba-version-1.
AMI: Amazon Linux 2023.
Instance type: t3.micro.
Key pair: Don't include in launch template.
Network settings: select existing security group fa-lba-web-sg.
Enable Auto-assign Public IP.
Advanced details: set IMDSv2 to Required.
Paste the supplied user-data.sh into User data.
Create the launch template and confirm version 1 exists.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - enter lab folder
cliBlocks.content: Set-Location "C:\aws-labs\fa-lba"

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - resolve latest AL2023 AMI
cliBlocks.content: $AMI_ID = aws ssm get-parameter --name /aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-x86_64 --query "Parameter.Value" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - rebuild web SG ID
cliBlocks.content: $WEB_SG_ID = aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=group-name,Values=fa-lba-web-sg --query "SecurityGroups[0].GroupId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - base64 user data
cliBlocks.content: $USER_DATA_B64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String([System.IO.File]::ReadAllBytes((Resolve-Path ".\user-data.sh")))

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - build launch template JSON
cliBlocks.content: $LT_DATA = @{ ImageId=$AMI_ID; InstanceType="t3.micro"; UserData=$USER_DATA_B64; MetadataOptions=@{HttpTokens="required";HttpEndpoint="enabled"}; NetworkInterfaces=@(@{DeviceIndex=0;AssociatePublicIpAddress=$true;DeleteOnTermination=$true;Groups=@($WEB_SG_ID)}); TagSpecifications=@(@{ResourceType="instance";Tags=@(@{Key="Name";Value="fa-lba-web"},@{Key="FollowAlong";Value="fa-lba"})}) } | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 8

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - save launch template JSON
cliBlocks.content: $LT_DATA | Set-Content -Encoding utf8 .\launch-template-data.json

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create launch template
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 create-launch-template --launch-template-name fa-lba-lt --version-description fa-lba-version-1 --launch-template-data file://launch-template-data.json --tag-specifications "ResourceType=launch-template,Tags=[{Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-lba}]" --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - verify launch template
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 describe-launch-template-versions --launch-template-name fa-lba-lt --versions 1 --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

editableBlocks.title: user-data.sh
editableBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash set -euxo pipefail dnf install -y httpd TOKEN=$(curl -sS -X PUT -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600" http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token) INSTANCE_ID=$(curl -sS -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: ${TOKEN}" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id) AZ=$(curl -sS -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: ${TOKEN}" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/placement/availability-zone) cat > /var/www/html/index.html < fa-lba

Load Balancing & Auto Scaling Follow Along

Instance: ${INSTANCE_ID}

Availability Zone: ${AZ}

EOF echo "healthy" > /var/www/html/health systemctl enable httpd systemctl start httpd

expectedResults: It uses t3.micro, the resolved AL2023 AMI, fa-lba-web-sg and IMDSv2 required.

verificationChecks.text: Public IPv4 is enabled for the primary network interface.

tasks.title: Create the Application Load Balancer and HTTP listener
tasks.goal: Create fa-lba-alb across the two public subnets and forward HTTP:80 to fa-lba-tg.
tasks.whyItMatters: The ALB is the single public Layer 7 entry point and forwards only to healthy targets.
tasks.examRelevance: ALB is the Layer 7 choice for HTTP/HTTPS application routing.
warnings: Application Load Balancers incur charges while running.

browserSteps.instruction: Open EC2 > Load Balancers > Create load balancer > Application Load Balancer.
Name: fa-lba-alb.
Scheme: Internet-facing.
IP address type: IPv4.
VPC: fa-lba-vpc.
Select eu-west-2a/fa-lba-public-a and eu-west-2b/fa-lba-public-b.
Security group: fa-lba-alb-sg only.
Listener: HTTP port 80.
Default action: Forward to fa-lba-tg.
Create the load balancer.
Wait until State is Active.
Copy the generated DNS name.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - rebuild subnet A ID
cliBlocks.content: $SUBNET_A_ID = aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-lba-public-a --query "Subnets[0].SubnetId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - rebuild subnet B ID
cliBlocks.content: $SUBNET_B_ID = aws ec2 describe-subnets --filters Name=tag:Name,Values=fa-lba-public-b --query "Subnets[0].SubnetId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - rebuild ALB SG ID
cliBlocks.content: $ALB_SG_ID = aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=group-name,Values=fa-lba-alb-sg --query "SecurityGroups[0].GroupId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - rebuild target group ARN
cliBlocks.content: $TG_ARN = aws elbv2 describe-target-groups --names fa-lba-tg --query "TargetGroups[0].TargetGroupArn" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create ALB
cliBlocks.content: $ALB_ARN = aws elbv2 create-load-balancer --name fa-lba-alb --type application --scheme internet-facing --ip-address-type ipv4 --subnets $SUBNET_A_ID $SUBNET_B_ID --security-groups $ALB_SG_ID --tags Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-lba --query "LoadBalancers[0].LoadBalancerArn" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait for ALB
cliBlocks.content: aws elbv2 wait load-balancer-available --load-balancer-arns $ALB_ARN --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create listener
cliBlocks.content: $LISTENER_ARN = aws elbv2 create-listener --load-balancer-arn $ALB_ARN --protocol HTTP --port 80 --default-actions Type=forward,TargetGroupArn=$TG_ARN --query "Listeners[0].ListenerArn" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - get ALB DNS
cliBlocks.content: $ALB_DNS = aws elbv2 describe-load-balancers --names fa-lba-alb --query "LoadBalancers[0].DNSName" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-lba-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - show ALB DNS
cliBlocks.content: Write-Output $ALB_DNS

expectedResults: An ALB DNS name is available.

verificationChecks.text: The listener default action points at fa-lba-tg.

tasks.title: Create the Auto Scaling group and attach the target group
tasks.goal: Create fa-lba-asg with Min 2, Desired 2 and Max 4 across both public subnets, attach fa-lba-tg, enable ELB health checks and use 120-second grace/warmup.
tasks.whyItMatters: The group maintains capacity across two Availability Zones and automatically registers every launched instance with the target group.
tasks.examRelevance: Horizontal scaling plus load-balancer health integration is a core elastic-compute design.
warnings: Allow several minutes for Apache installation and initial health checks before diagnosing failure.

browserSteps.instruction: Open EC2 > Auto Scaling Groups > Create Auto Scaling group.
Name: fa-lba-asg.
Launch template: fa-lba-lt, version 1.
VPC: fa-lba-vpc.
Select fa-lba-public-a and fa-lba-public-b.
Attach to an existing load balancer target group and choose fa-lba-tg.
Turn on Elastic Load Balancing health checks.
Health check grace period: 120 seconds.
Desired capacity: 2.

Maximum capacity: 4.

Add Name=fa-lba-web and propagate it to instances.
Create the group.
Wait for two instances to become InService.
Open fa-lba-tg > Targets and wait for both targets to become Healthy.

tasks.examRelevance: For request-driven web workloads, request count per target can connect scaling directly to backend load.

browserSteps.instruction: Open fa-lba-asg > Automatic scaling.

Name: fa-lba-request-scaling.

Target value: 50.
Select the fa-lba-alb/fa-lba-tg metric resource.
Keep scale in enabled.
Create the policy.

tasks.title: Generate controlled traffic and observe scale-out
tasks.goal: Run the five-minute request generator and observe fa-lba-asg scale above its initial desired capacity of 2 without exceeding 4.
tasks.whyItMatters: A scaling policy is meaningful only when metric pressure can be connected to scaling activities and newly healthy targets.
tasks.examRelevance: Target tracking follows changing demand and accounts for instance warmup.
warnings: The generator is limited to five minutes; stop it once scale-out is proven.
CloudWatch timing and 120-second warmup mean scaling is not instantaneous.

browserSteps.instruction: Open fa-lba-asg > Activity so scaling events are visible.
Open Automatic scaling in another tab and confirm fa-lba-request-scaling is enabled.
Open PowerShell in C:\aws-labs\fa-lba.
Get the ALB DNS name.
Run .\generate-load.ps1 -AlbDnsName $ALB_DNS.
Let the generator run for up to five minutes.
Refresh Activity every minute.
When a scale-out event appears, note the new Desired capacity.
Wait for any new instance to become InService.
Open fa-lba-tg > Targets and wait for the new target to become Healthy.
Press Ctrl+C once scale-out above 2 is proven; do not generate unnecessary traffic.
Scale-in may take additional minutes and does not need to finish before Task 13.

tasks.title: Review the SAA-C03 load balancing and Auto Scaling decisions
tasks.goal: Translate the completed architecture into exam rules and common distinctions.
tasks.whyItMatters: SAA-C03 tests architecture selection more than console sequence memory.
tasks.examRelevance: ALB, target groups, launch templates, Auto Scaling, target tracking and health checks are directly relevant to elastic compute design.

browserSteps.instruction: ALB is Layer 7 for HTTP/HTTPS application traffic.
A listener receives traffic; a target group routes to and health-checks backend targets.
The ALB SG accepts client HTTP; the web SG accepts HTTP only from the ALB SG.
A launch template defines reusable EC2 instance configuration.
An ASG manages minimum, desired and maximum capacity across multiple subnets/AZs.
Horizontal scaling adds/removes instances; vertical scaling changes instance size.
Target tracking tries to keep a chosen metric near a target value.
ALBRequestCountPerTarget is useful when requests per backend represent load.
Target-group health controls routing eligibility.
ASG ELB health integration can replace load-balancer-unhealthy instances after the grace period.
Health-check grace period protects a new instance during startup.
Default instance warmup prevents initializing capacity being treated as fully ready for scaling decisions.
Exam trigger: HTTP host/path routing points to ALB.
Exam trigger: automatic EC2 capacity changes point to ASG plus scaling policy.
Exam trigger: multi-AZ resilience points to ALB and ASG spanning multiple AZs.
Exam trap: healthy EC2 system checks do not prove the application is healthy at /health.

troubleshooting.title: Targets never become healthy
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Apache installation/user data is not complete, outbound internet is unavailable, or the web security group does not allow the ALB security group.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the subnet default route/public IPv4, then verify fa-lba-web-sg allows TCP 80 from fa-lba-alb-sg and allow the grace period plus initial health checks.

troubleshooting.title: Target health shows 404
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The configured health-check path does not exist.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm fa-lba-tg uses /health and user-data.sh writes /var/www/html/health.

troubleshooting.title: ALB DNS returns 503
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The listener has no healthy target.
troubleshooting.fix: Open fa-lba-tg Targets and resolve target health before changing the listener.

troubleshooting.title: ASG cannot launch instances
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Launch template, subnet or service-linked-role/EC2 permissions are invalid.
troubleshooting.fix: Read the exact ASG Activity failure, verify fa-lba-lt version 1 and both subnet IDs, then confirm the IAM policy permissions.

troubleshooting.title: Scaling policy does not scale out
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Request volume was not sustained long enough or new capacity is still warming.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm ALBRequestCountPerTarget target 50, run the supplied generator for several minutes and review scaling activities before changing the target.

troubleshooting.title: Security group cannot be deleted
troubleshooting.likelyCause: An ALB or EC2 ENI still references it.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify zero ASG instances, delete the ALB and wait for ENIs to disappear, then retry only the exact fa-lba security group.

troubleshooting.title: VPC cannot be deleted
troubleshooting.likelyCause: A subnet, route table, internet gateway, security group or ENI dependency remains.
troubleshooting.fix: Recheck reverse dependency cleanup and remove only the remaining fa-lba dependency.
